title: Room vs silos: hill-climbing with three Haiku 5.5 agents
summary: Does sharing a Playbox room help small agents find a hidden vector? Same code, prompt, boxes and budget; only what each agent can see differs.

config.task: hidden integer vector; score = squared distance + 2x sum gap

samples_note: Per-try scores.tsv files are not committed; samples are per-trial finals (row 4) and per-checkpoint means (row 5) from docs/benchmark.md.

timeline.text: Sharing helps when the work is split: the room is the only condition that ends with one usable combined answer (posted vector 48.6k vs 108.1k, p = 0.0002).
Sharing did not clearly help when every agent can score everything; a classical random hill-climber beats the model runs on the plain task.
Per dollar, many cheap tries beat an expensive advisor: $0.79 of Haiku tries solved every slice in 4 of 4 trials; $1.18 of advisor calls reached 0 in half.
Small samples (3 to 8 trials per condition). Read the p-values, not just the means.
No room arm in row 5: whether sharing helps a cheap swarm was not run.
Several room trials were stopped by a time limit at 82 to 89 of 90 tries and counted (rule: at least 80 of 90 and no invalid tries).
